correctness.rationale: The primal facets are complements of disconnected four-sets and the dual faces avoid such sets. An independent Cayley-graph check used the quotient of the five-cube by the all-ones vector, giving four basis generators plus their sum. It reproduced 680 connected four-sets and 1140 disconnected ones, 192 five-faces and no six-face, so the primal is pure of dimension eleven and the dual has the claimed face vector. Coordinates on triangles away from vertex 0 give an integral isomorphism from the dual two-cycle lattice to Z^455: a basis consists of boundaries of formal tetrahedra through vertex 0. The independent pivot rounds of sizes 170,140,145 give a triangular unit minor for d3, proving integral surjectivity. The 192 four-cells have 480 shared tetrahedra with two incidences each, and 200 tetrahedra have no incidence; propagation of signs gave coherent orientation on a connected incidence graph. Hence d4 becomes the transpose of the graph incidence matrix with zero rows added, rank 191 and primitive image (a spanning tree gives a unit minor). This yields dual H3=Z^34 and H4=Z. The dual three-skeleton is simply connected by its full two-skeleton and is two-connected by d3 surjectivity and Hurewicz. It is therefore equivalent to 225 three-spheres. The four-cell attaching maps are a wedge map from 192 three-spheres, classified on each sphere by its integral degree vector. Both basis changes in its Smith reduction are realized by wedge homotopy equivalences. The cofiber of the 191 unit components cancels those pairs, leaving 34 three-spheres and one four-sphere. Duality on sixteen labels shifts the nonzero homology to primal degrees nine and ten, with no torsion. Lower-degree homology obstructs pure shellability.
residual_risks: The wedge conclusion is for the Alexander dual; no original-complex homotopy wedge is asserted.

evidence: The other record uses the four-bit Cayley graph with generators 1,2,4,8,15. In the frozen five-bit even subspace, the edge differences are g_i=11111 XOR e_i for i=1,...,5. Their only nontrivial subset relation over F2 is the sum of all five: an even-size sum vanishes only for the empty subset, and an odd-size sum vanishes only when all five e_i are present. Mapping g_1,...,g_4 to the four unit vectors maps g_5 to 15 and is a graph isomorphism.
Both definitions complement precisely the disconnected induced four-sets; the relabelling thus gives simplicial isomorphisms of the cut complexes and their combinatorial Alexander duals.
